approach.method_basis: The Parent walks from one scored molecular graph. It samples local atom and bond edits, including direct exchanges of an aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same six-member ring. Valid, canonically fresh neighbors pass through a short-lived inverse-motif memory before filling the announced batch. The walk moves to the highest-scoring accepted neighbor even when that score is worse than its source, breaks exact score ties by canonical spelling, and keeps a separate best archive. Each selected transition installs at most four inverse local-motif restrictions. Installation first reserves up to two slots for each sign, then fills any remaining slots by occurrence-change magnitude and canonical motif order. A candidate is vetoed only if it matches both inverse signs from the same selected transition. Overlapping keys take the latest provenance and deadline, entries expire after four completed steps, and a documented oldest-entry release handles generation obstruction. Normalized canonical identities preserve the proposal-to-feedback join.
approach.novelty: Remove the sign reservation from the four-slot installation choice. Select the four highest-ranked changed motifs using the Parent's existing magnitude and canonical ordering, irrespective of how many have each sign. Keep insertion order unchanged whenever the selected keys agree with the Parent. This isolates the contribution of sign-balanced memory allocation to a veto that already requires both signs. Earlier siblings changed which motifs rank first while retaining the sign reservation, changed matching or memory lifetime, or removed the whole veto or nitrogen-relocation menu. None removed this reservation alone. The Parent trace suggests that most changed selections would still retain both signs, so the utility prediction is non-inferiority, not stronger chemical credit or a guaranteed reduction in vetoes. Actual memory and admission changes will establish execution; complete scored trajectories will test that prediction.

observed_bottleneck: Parent n-abcd951ab7cc allocates a bounded inverse-memory budget by reserving up to two slots per sign before applying its magnitude/canonical ranking. This forces sign balance even where an unrestricted choice would still supply the two signs required by the same-transition veto; the continuing contribution of the reservation is unresolved. Its actual three summary.json and run.log pairs confirm complete evaluations, macro mean 0.5217591163770486 and population SD 0.006329100643035156. The aromatic-relocation Parent gain over n-9f7c7ec50039 is only 0.0008412882577690054 with mixed seed effects, and that addition remains intact here. A read-only reconstruction from all Parent motif definitions, selected-transition changes, installations, expirations and checked candidate attempts exactly reproduces its 195 vetoes among 4545 valid-novel tests. On the 420 installations followed by further proposals, global top-four selection under the unchanged within-sign rank changes 115 selected key sets and replaces 116 slots. Both signs are retained at 414 installations rather than the Parent's 415. Sixty-five four-slot selections move from two negative changes to one, forty-nine move from two to three, and one moves from two to zero. Mean summed absolute occurrence change changes only from 4.2404761904761905 to 4.242857142857143, with a strict increase at just one installation; the evidence does not support a general stronger-magnitude claim. A conditional alternate memory replay on the recorded Parent transitions and candidate stream gives 190 vetoes, with ten relaxed and five added decisions across fourteen batches. These are passive membership and predicate calculations, not alternate evaluated batches or an independently evolving walk. Two further changed installations are terminal and cannot affect later proposals. Published integration removals n-045725e4628f and n-b17e822169e2 lost paired endpoint means by 0.0022752593461056922 and 0.0029650200850093547 when removing veto enforcement and overlap refresh. Those failures warn that sparse admission changes can matter. Credit-ranking siblings n-f37b5cf41e6f and n-612eae72dd0d retained sign quotas and lost mean endpoints by 0.002455559942229346 and 0.0010689328980496942. They do not isolate this reservation's contribution.
hypothesis: Remove the per-sign reservation from bounded inverse-motif installation: select up to the inherited four changed motifs by the Parent's global descending absolute occurrence-change and canonical-motif rank without sign quotas, preserving inherited insertion order on coincident selections and retaining the same-transition bidirectional veto and memory lifecycle.

finding_summary.headline: Removing sign balance changed search and lost 0.01185 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: Keeping both signs available is not enough to preserve the contribution of balanced memory allocation. Which motif representatives inherit each transition’s provenance matters even when capacity, magnitude ranking, veto logic and memory lifetime stay fixed. Ten relaxed admissions produced only one source improvement, one tie and eight losses, with no immediate archive gains; most changed the batch cutoff without becoming the next state. Conversely, one added veto enabled an oxygen-deletion refill that did improve the zaleplon archive. These opposing local effects show why fewer vetoes cannot stand in for better search. The loss supports retaining the quota in the developed method on this panel, while leaving the responsible individual replacements unresolved: ten conditional comparison batches lack a tenth recorded member, and passive memories do not define independently evolved walks or scores. Chemistry remained in the same aromatic/carbonyl, aryl-amine and sulfur-cage families, with nearly unchanged size and persistent reactive heteroatom bonds and unspecified stereochemistry. The observed score tradeoff therefore does not establish improved chemical feasibility.
finding_summary.results: The removal executed exactly and changed 116 of 420 memory installations that could affect later proposals. Most still retained both signs: 414 of 420, while total selected motif-change magnitude increased by only one count. On the Child’s recorded history, restoring balanced selection would change twelve gate decisions: ten candidates were newly admitted by the removal and two were newly vetoed. This reached actual scored allocation and selected states. Eight of fifteen task/seed trajectories changed; all fifteen finished. The three-seed mean final Top-1 score fell from 0.521759 to 0.509908, a paired loss of 0.011851 that exceeds the allowed 0.002 decline. Seed effects were +0.009516, -0.041309 and -0.003760. Sitagliptin supplied the largest loss, especially seed 1 at -0.195597, and DRD2 also declined; zaleplon improved. Mean recorded AUC fell from 0.393354 to 0.391556. The mechanism is confirmed, and the non-inferiority prediction is rejected.

molecular.headline: Aromatic carbonyls and aryl amines persist, with reactive N/O bonds, unusual sulfur coordination and densely fused cages
molecular.overall_character: Every supplied child and parent trajectory was read, and all requested tasks are covered. Each task contains 900 recorded molecules, including 870 optimizer proposals. The proposal ring-closure-token rate is 1.0 throughout, aromatic-token rates range from 0.7977 to 1.0, and mean SMILES lengths range from 46.3 to 70.1. These are molecular string readings rather than fractions of aromatic atoms or tests of chemical stability. The output consists of substantial ring-bearing compounds: indole/benzofuran amides and aryl ketones, bulky decorated aza-heterocycles, halogenated aryl amines, bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems and highly fused sulfur cages. Distinct seed families give moderate structural diversity, while the strongest excerpts remain concentrated in closely related frameworks. Typical heavy-atom sizes are unchanged from parent n-abcd951ab7cc, and 7 of the 15 task/seed trajectories are identical. Changed trajectories retain the same broad chemistry and its unresolved liabilities rather than showing uniformly more conventional structures. Ordinary amides, amines, ethers and carbonyls coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, N-N/N-O bridges, peroxides, sulfur-halogen bonds and multiply bonded sulfur with additional substituents or hydrogen. All charged-token and stereocentre-token rates are 0.0. Neutral strings do not establish solution protonation, and unassigned configurations do not imply achiral structures. Size and structural counts below are passive RDKit readings of supplied SMILES; no new oracle score, synthesis score or geometric-feasibility result was generated. Local score associations do not reveal an unseen required scaffold or prove that chemically questionable bonds are necessary.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 21-29 heavy atoms. The strongest families combine fused aromatic or partly unsaturated rings with an aryl amide or aryl ketone. The leading benzofuran-like carboxanilide bears methyl groups, thiol, an amino-chloromethyl group and an N-chloro amide. Another strong molecule is a comparatively ordinary ethoxy/methyl/thiol indole carboxanilide. The changed seed-0 leaders are indene-like aminopyridyl ketones bearing methoxy and N-fluoroaminomethyl substituents, with optional carbon-bound fluorine. Their aromatic nitrogen chemistry is clearly present. Low molecules enlarge or interrupt the fused ring system, lose aromatic organization or replace the carbonyl connection. The ordinary amide and ketone fragments are plausible synthetic motifs, while the reactive nitrogen substituents and dense bridged derivatives make the full set questionable.
liabilities: N-Cl amide, N-F/N-O groups and amino-chloromethyl functionality are distinct concerns from ordinary aryl halogenation.
Thiols, dense ring closures and unusual sulfur connections occur in alternative families.
Late bridged molecules add N-N functionality and further ring complexity without defining configuration.
missing_features: The weaker expanded-ring and carbonyl-replaced molecules lack the compact aromatic/carbonyl organization retained in stronger compounds.
Conventional amine and N-H amide counterparts around the reactive leading frameworks remain incompletely represented, although an ordinary indole amide already scores nearby.
Configurations at substituted saturated sites and bridged junctions remain unspecified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The N-chloro benzofuran derivative scores 0.41003927643747895, the new aminopyridyl ketone 0.40497388700123543, its close relative 0.3996288825296233, and the conventional indole N-H amide 0.39905049777278273. An expanded, partly dearomatized ring derivative retaining an aminopyridyl ketone scores 0.029932041552435174, and a carbonyl-replaced indole derivative scores 0.03343008011310944. The higher scores associate with the compact aromatic/carbonyl arrangement, rather than simply adding nitrogen or retaining molecular size. Bridged N-H amide relatives with carbon-bound chlorine or bromine both score 0.3900523103411983, and the corresponding dehalogenated relative scores 0.385823971421255. Current seed 0 changes from the parent benzothiophene-like ketone at 0.393567030299894 to the aminopyridyl ketone at 0.40497388700123543. Seeds 1 and 2 are identical to the parent. The new stronger family still has an N-F bond, so the score change does not resolve local chemical reactivity.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 30-53 heavy atoms, with a median of 38 as in the parent. The leading 51-heavy-atom molecule joins an extensively substituted aryl group to a fused nitrogen heterocycle bearing carbonyl and thiocarbonyl functions. Imine groups, an amino-fluoroalkyl connection, a long mixed ether/thioether chain and a multiply bonded, additionally substituted sulfur centre make the molecule highly elaborate. N-bromo and terminal S-Cl relatives appear in the leading series. The final seed-2 family instead combines an aza-aromatic dione with unsaturated carbon substituents and a fused aza/ether ring carrying acetal-like branching. The changed seed-1 family contains an unsaturated aza-carbonyl framework and an aryl acyl-sulfur-acyl linkage. Low examples retain ester/phenol/aza-carbonyl fragments but alter heterocyclic conjugation or ring connectivity. Familiar fragments abound, while reactive bonds and long appendages weaken practical simplicity and stability.
liabilities: N-Br and S-Cl bonds, imines and multiply bonded substituted sulfur complicate stability and synthesis.
Long mixed ether/thioether chains and extensive branching increase flexibility and assembly demands.
The changed acyl-sulfur-acyl linkage introduces reactive acyl functionality even though the parent O-F group is absent.
missing_features: The lower altered-ring molecules lack the same preserved heterocyclic organization as the stronger decorated families.
Matched compact relatives with stable linkers remain incomplete; equal scores do not show a need for N-bromination, extra side-chain branching or greater alkyl length.
Configuration at fluorinated and acetal-like carbon sites and geometry of unsaturated substituents remain undefined.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading decorated structure scores 0.6161710037174721. Multiple relatives share exactly 0.6155070237050044 despite alkyl extension, side-chain branching or replacement of N-methyl by N-bromo. Two final aza/ether-ring variants likewise share 0.6092182584436399 with different oxygen/sulfur-containing appendages. The score therefore distinguishes the retained decorated heterocyclic organization more clearly than several individual peripheral modifications. Early altered-ring examples score 0.526081691583997 and 0.5286081645773063, below the initial aromatic dione at 0.548381482770623. Seeds 0 and 2 exactly reproduce the parent. The new seed-1 maximum is 0.5941905687894993 versus parental 0.605139548855754, with the acyl-sulfur-acyl family replacing the parental amidine/thioester family carrying an O-F substituent. No O-halogen bond is found in the current proposals, versus 70 parent proposals with one, but N-Br, S-Cl and unusual sulfur coordination remain. Losing that particular liability does not establish overall chemical feasibility.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 31-43 heavy atoms, with a median of 36. All proposal strings contain aromatic and halogen tokens. The leading family combines a tolyl group, a fused nitrogen/sulfur ring system, a fluorinated pyrrolidine and an amino/chloro-substituted aryl group. A ring-size/connectivity variant contains a fluorinated piperidine instead. The sulfur-rich fused framework retains a sulfur-sulfur multiple bond and multiply bonded S-H environments. Another seed gives small nitrogen/sulfur rings linked to halogenated aryl thiocarbonyl groups, thiol and sulfur-chlorine functionality; a third retains a highly fused aryl/amine/sulfur family. Low molecules remain acid/amide/sulfonamide derivatives of the initial biaryl structure, with fewer accessible aliphatic amines. Recognizable aryl and amine fragments are present, but the assembled sulfur bonding and undefined ring geometry remain highly questionable.
liabilities: Sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds, multiply bonded S-H centres and sulfur-halogen bonds are difficult stability and synthesis features.
Small or fused nitrogen/sulfur rings require specific geometric relationships.
The leading carbon/sulfur pair has four and five unassigned tetrahedral centres, respectively, in passive RDKit readings.
missing_features: The low acid/amide/sulfonamide molecules lack the accessible aliphatic-amine and aryl-linker organization of the stronger products.

Stable conventional-valence ring and linker alternatives preserving that organization remain incomplete. Several exact carbon/sulfur ties show that extra sulfur is optional at particular observed sites.
Basic-centre protonation and configurations of fluorinated rings, fused junctions and possible stereogenic sulfur environments remain unresolved.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Carbon/sulfur alternatives at a fused-ring position share the highest observed score, 0.8960118866009306. Other matched carbon/sulfur substitutions share 0.8500094650652374 or 0.8302140284961123. These ties do not support a requirement for sulfur at those particular sites. The fluorinated piperidine variant scores 0.8754206840254091, adding a methyl group to the leading pyrrolidine gives 0.8525332066418447, and substituting sulfur for carbon within that pyrrolidine gives 0.8150395448985218. Removing its aryl chlorine gives 0.7120528839225895. The local arrangement matters; more sulfur, bulk or generic amine content is not uniformly useful. A low acid/amide/sulfonamide derivative scores 0.007468397818197266. The stronger association remains connected aryl/aliphatic-amine chemistry rather than aromatic content alone. Current seed-0 and seed-2 maxima are 0.8500094650652374 and 0.8960118866009306, versus parental 0.8856242185485628 and 0.9148143511682032; seed 1 is identical. Sulfur-halogen-bearing proposals increase from 26 to 121, so the changed chemistry retains or intensifies this liability despite similar molecular size.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 27-45 heavy atoms, with a median of 35 as in the parent. The leading series combines an alkyl-substituted aza-aromatic ring, an aryl group and a bridged nitrogen/carbonyl framework containing an N-N-O connection. The highest observed molecule has 30 heavy atoms. Close relatives alter carbonyl-to-nitrogen spacing, add methyl or hydroxymethyl groups, insert a peroxide, or introduce multiply bonded sulfur at an unsaturated aryl connection. Other seeds retain brominated aryl compounds with O-Br bonds and N-N/carbonyl rings, or expanded N/O/S ring systems with pyridyl, phenolic, aldehyde and carbonyl functionality. The low examples include ring-opened carbonyl-chain derivatives and highly substituted reactive aryl heterocycles. Familiar individual fragments coexist with demanding bridged topology and labile-looking heteroatom sequences.
liabilities: N-N/O connections and occasional peroxides add context-dependent reactivity concerns to complex ring systems.
O-Br and unusually substituted sulfur persist in other families.
Dense bridges and expanded ring paths impose synthetic and conformational demands.
missing_features: The weaker ring-opened or extensively altered derivatives lack the constrained aromatic/carbonyl organization of the stronger series.

Less labile bridge alternatives preserving that organization remain incompletely covered. The similar scores of N-O, N-N-O and peroxide relatives do not establish a necessity for the longest heteroatom sequence.
Bridged-junction configuration and accessible conformations of the expanded heterocycles are not specified.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The leading N-N-O-bridged polycycle scores 0.20981104279018886. A shorter carbonyl-to-ring connection scores 0.20775769309691736; a related N-O bridge without the extra nitrogen scores 0.2056349053193895, and a peroxide-containing relative scores 0.20647766243219587. These nearby values associate the broad constrained aryl/carbonyl arrangement with stronger scores more clearly than a requirement for any specific reactive bridge. Adding a methyl substituent to the leading framework gives 0.20754851593468432. Ring-opened carbonyl-chain molecules score 0.12467972074136988 and 0.1263981386214515, while a flexible O-Br/sulfur-containing aryl derivative scores 0.12870267321446027. The parent seed-0 leader has a related N-O bridge and a different alkyl substitution pattern at 0.21196904390980506, versus current 0.20981104279018886. Seed 1 is identical; seed 2 retains the same earlier maximum 0.20185639717998205 despite different later chemistry. Current N-N-containing proposals increase to 409 from 257 in the parent, without a corresponding disappearance of the existing ring and reactivity concerns.

per_task.generated_character: The proposals contain 25-36 heavy atoms, with a median of 29, but their ring topology is exceptionally dense. The leading molecule has 31 heavy atoms, six sulfur atoms and seven RDKit-perceived rings. Its cage incorporates a nitrogen-containing dione, another carbonyl, fluorinated carbon sites, N-S/N-N connections, multiply bonded substituted sulfur and several S-H-containing ring environments. Closely related structures replace carbon atoms by sulfur while retaining the same broad cage. Other strong examples rearrange that cage or alter a carbonyl; the unchanged seed-2 family contains aldehyde and N-fluoroimino functionality in a different sulfur cage. Low molecules include both expanded aromatic diones and other already sulfur-rich, heavily fused compounds. Carbonyl presence is universal in the current proposal set, so the chemistry is not missing carbonyl groups in general. The specific placement, ring geometry and stability are the unresolved issues.
liabilities: Multiply bonded substituted sulfur, S-H-containing rings and N-S/N-N connections make stability and practical synthesis highly uncertain.
The leading molecule has six unassigned tetrahedral centres; the doubly sulfur-substituted relative has nine in passive RDKit readings.
Alternative cages contain N-F, sulfur-halogen, aldehyde or imino functionality in addition to their geometric constraints.

Conventional-valence, less constrained alternatives retaining that polar-group arrangement are missing from the leading excerpt. The matched carbon/sulfur comparisons support exploring fewer unusual sulfur sites, not assuming the entire cage is chemically necessary.
Fluorinated carbon sites and cage junctions lack assigned configuration or demonstrated accessible three-dimensional structures.

Replacing a carbon at one ring site by sulfur gives 0.5501235427929417; a sulfur substitution at another site gives 0.5294960909652826; the corresponding structure with both replacements scores 0.51263066071853. More sulfur is therefore not favored in these matched local comparisons. Replacing a carbonyl by imino functionality in the latter framework gives 0.4588793078849804. Converting a methyl-bearing saturated site to an exocyclic methylene in a related cage changes 0.5501235427929417 to 0.45334584680577134. Exact polar-group and saturation patterns matter. An early expanded aromatic dione scores 7.590554525032884e-10, and another densely connected fluorinated sulfur framework scores 6.45202455128507e-09; sulfur, rings and fluorine alone do not explain the stronger scores. Current seed 0 reaches 0.5551309966222325 versus parental 0.48118636011729826 with a different sulfur cage. Seed 1 reaches an aldehyde-bearing fused sulfur family at 0.3947560744548977, versus the parent fluorinated dione cage at 0.5903526424693334. Seed 2 is identical at 0.4484554129767839. The molecular evidence changes the preferred cage arrangement without demonstrating improved chemical feasibility.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Cited molecules contain N-halogen, O-Br, sulfur-halogen, N-N/N-O and peroxide connections, as well as sulfur-sulfur multiple bonds. Carbon/sulfur alternatives share 0.8960118866009306, 0.8500094650652374 or 0.8302140284961123. In a separate cage series, the six-sulfur member scores 0.5551309966222325 versus 0.5501235427929417, 0.5294960909652826 and 0.51263066071853 after additional carbon-to-sulfur replacements.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful ring and polar-group arrangements remain coupled to reactive heteroatom bonds and unusually coordinated sulfur.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make stable matched linkers and conventional atom environments accessible while preserving the useful fragment arrangement. Distinguish ordinary sulfur groups and carbon-bound halogens from unusual sulfur coordination or heteroatom-halogen bonds; evaluate chemically simpler carbon or conventional nitrogen alternatives without excluding whole elements.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A compact aminopyridyl ketone scores 0.3996288825296233 while an expanded, partly dearomatized relative scores 0.029932041552435174. A fluorinated nitrogen-ring family scores 0.8960118866009306, versus 0.8754206840254091 after changing ring size/connectivity and 0.8150395448985218 after a carbon-to-sulfur replacement within the ring. Carbonyl-rich open-chain derivatives elsewhere remain below their constrained aryl/carbonyl relatives.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring expansion and atom replacement do not consistently preserve the geometry and conjugation associated with stronger molecules.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide controlled linker-length, ring-size and attachment-position comparisons that retain the other useful features. Include feasible ordinary ring systems and preserve conjugated carbonyl placement instead of treating generic ring or heteroatom content as an adequate substitute for molecular organization.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Decorated heterocycles share exactly 0.6155070237050044 across alkyl extension, branching and N-methyl-to-N-bromo changes. Oxygen/sulfur appendage variants share 0.6092182584436399. Adding a methyl group to a bridged carbonyl framework changes 0.20981104279018886 to 0.20754851593468432.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output lacks complete simpler counterparts where added branches, chain length or reactive substitutions have little observed local benefit.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Include coherent branch deletion, chain shortening and replacement of unnecessary reactive connections while holding the principal scaffold fixed. Use actual feedback to determine which compact alternatives retain the useful chemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every charged-token and stereocentre-token rate is 0.0. The leading carbon/sulfur aryl-amine pair has four and five unassigned tetrahedral centres, while the leading sulfur cage has six and a close sulfur-enriched cage has nine. Other cited structures include acetal-like carbon sites, imines and bridged N/O systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereochemical identity and plausible molecular states remain undefined for constrained, ionizable products.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Specify and preserve feasible configurations at substituted rings and junctions, and account for relevant double-bond geometry, tautomerism and protonation. Couple that representation to less constrained matched frameworks; graph validity alone does not demonstrate an accessible stereoisomer or solution-state identity.

method_name: Tabu search: de novo graph walks with expiring structural prohibitions
method_thesis: The anchor is the basic tabu-search procedure in Section 2 of [Glover, Tabu Search—Part I](https://leeds-faculty.colorado.edu/glover/TS%20-%20Part%20I-ORSA-aw.pdf), fixed before locating this external source. It chooses the best available admissible move, including a worsening move, while temporarily prohibiting reversals through short-term attribute memory. My molecular adaptation starts from the best supplied observation and maintains one current molecular graph, its true score, an independent best-observed archive, and expiring structural restrictions. At each feedback step, stochastically generate a new neighborhood through atom and bond edits, additions, deletions and chemically checked ring changes. Define move attributes from presence/absence changes of canonical local subgraphs around the edited region. After selecting a move, temporarily forbid a bounded record of its inverse attribute changes. These restrictions must apply to different canonical molecules sharing the affected local chemistry, so they can alter search beyond the protocol's mandatory whole-molecule duplicate rejection. Generate valid, canonical-unique, admissible neighbors until the announced batch is filled, then submit them directly without a learned score predictor. Only after real feedback choose the highest-scoring accepted neighbor as the next current graph, even when it scores below the current graph; retain the best score seen anywhere. Age restrictions by completed walk steps. If restrictions prevent sufficient fresh generation, release the oldest restrictions only as needed and record that release. This root uses the basic tabu form without an aspiration rule requiring unknown candidate scores. Preparation needs no learned model or corpus molecule store. Each objective restarts the same task-agnostic procedure with clean labeled and tabu state, and every proposed structure is generated online from the evolving current graph. The hypothesis is that an aggressive observed-neighbor choice combined with temporary structural reversal restrictions can move through useful intermediate structures and reach higher scoring molecular regions within the supplied feedback schedule. Activation requires restrictions to veto otherwise valid novel structural moves and thereby influence later current states. That diagnostic is insufficient by itself: success is the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Overbroad attributes may suppress productive chemistry, while overly specific attributes may never affect novel proposals; the root must expose both possibilities.
